pages.title: Turning an intro lesson into a student

text.text: Most people who walk into a school for a free lesson decide within a week whether to join. The intro lesson is the school's whole sales process, so it is run by an instructor, never improvised.
Send the waiver with the booking text, so nobody fills in forms while the child waits.
Tell the instructor the student's age and anything the parent mentioned: shy, energetic, being bullied, needs focus. That is the reason they came.

Thirty minutes, one-to-one or in a small group. Bow in, teach three simple techniques, play one game, and finish with something the student can show their family at home. For adults, finish with a drill that makes them sweat a little and laugh a little.
Sit down with the parent or adult student, away from the door.
Ask what they noticed. Connect it to the reason they came.
Recommend one program and one schedule, not a menu. Twice a week is right for most beginners.
Offer the trial month. If they say yes, press
and assign the follow-up to yourself. Call within two days. Ask what would make it work: a different class time, a sibling discount, a friend joining too. If the answer is no, mark it
and leave a note; many families come back in the autumn.
